notes.title: Organization and nature of business
text: Note
1 – Organization and nature of business
E-Smart Corp.
(“Company,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) was incorporated on June 6, 2023, under the laws of
the State of Nevada, USA. E-Smart Corp. operates a digital platform for tattoo artist discovery and design. Our platform provides a catalog
of tattoo artists, with profiles that allow prospective clients to review artists’ work. We also publish monthly tattoo related
news and information to keep users informed about industry developments, tattoo styles, new materials, and innovations.
The Company
also offers AI Tattoo Generator (the “AI Tattoo Idea Generator API”), a digital tool that generates tattoo sketch concepts
from user input. The AI Tattoo Idea Generator is available to individual users through the Company’s website and to businesses and
developers through the AI Tattoo Idea Generator API, which is offered under paid subscription plans. Subscriptions to the AI Tattoo Idea
Generator API are currently the Company’s sole source of revenue.
The Company’s
principal executive office is located in Barcelona, Spain, from which its sole officer manages the Company’s operations.

notes.title: Going Concern
text: Note
2 – Going Concern
The accompanying financial statements have been prepared
in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles, which contemplate continuation of the Company as a going concern. The Company
currently has losses and has not completed its efforts to establish a stabilized source of revenues sufficient to cover operating costs
over an extended period of time. Therefore, there is substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern.
Management anticipates that the Company will be dependent, for the near future, on additional investment capital to fund operating expenses.
The Company intends to position itself so that it will be able to raise additional funds through the capital markets. In light of management’s
efforts, there are no assurances that the Company will be successful in this or any of its endeavors or become financially viable and
continue as a going concern.
E-Smart Corp.
has generated $ 42,870 of revenue and incurred a net loss of $ 127,976 for the year ended August 31, 2026, additionally, it’s reporting
an accumulated deficit since inception of $ 238,225 as of August 31, 2026.
The Company's capacity to operate as a going concern
is reliant on its ability to generate profitable operations in the future and/or secure the required funding to meet its obligations and
settle liabilities resulting from standard business operations when they become due. Management plans to finance operating expenses for
the next twelve months through loans from the Company’s Chief Executive Officer and/or a private offering of common stock. As of
August 31, 2026, the Company
had cash of $601, a working capital deficit of $258,426
and $65,245 of remaining availability under the related party loan agreement, under which the outstanding balance is repayable upon the
lender’s request. Net cash used in operating activities was $ 60,188 for the year ended August 31, 2026. The Company has no commitments
for additional financing, and management’s plans do not alleviate the substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue
as a going concern.

text: Note
3 – Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
Basis of presentation
The accompanying financial statements have been prepared
in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America. The Company’s year end is August 31.
Use of Estimates
The preparation of financial statements in conformity
with generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of
assets and liabilities and disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date the financial statements and the reported amount
of revenues and expenses during the reporting period. Actual results could differ from those estimates.
Foreign Currency
The Company’s functional and reporting currency
is the U.S. dollar. Transactions denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar (principally the euro) are remeasured into U.S.
dollars at the exchange rates in effect on the transaction dates, and monetary assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currencies
are remeasured at period-end exchange rates. Foreign currency transaction gains and losses are included in the statements of operations.
Fair
Value of Financial Instruments
FASB ASC Topic
820, "Fair Value Measurement," defines fair value as the exchange price that would be received for an asset
or paid to transfer a liability in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between
market participants on the measurement date. The standards apply to recurring and nonrecurring fair value measurements of financial and
non-financial assets and liabilities. The Company determines the fair values of its assets and liabilities based on a fair value hierarchy
that includes three levels of inputs that may be used to measure fair value.

notes.title: Related Party
text: Note 6 – Related Party
Effective June 6, 2023, the Company entered into a
loan agreement with Diana Vasylenko, the Company’s President, Chief Executive Officer, Treasurer, Secretary and Director. The agreement
established a Loan Amount of $70,000. The parties amended the agreement on November 14, 2023, increasing the Loan Amount to $220,000,
and on January 30, 2026, increasing it to $320,000. The loan has a stated interest rate of 0% and provides for no contractual interest
or fees. The agreement states that the loan is to be repaid over five years. The agreement provides for repayment from Company revenues
after the Company achieves “significant financial returns” and permits repayment upon the lender’s request.
As of August 31, 2026 and 2025, the amount due to
a related party was $ 254,755 and $ 200,790 , respectively. The loan is due on demand and is therefore classified as a current liability.
As of August 31, 2026, $65,245 of the $320,000 facility remained available.
The Company imputes interest on the loan at a market
rate and records it as interest expense with a corresponding credit to additional paid-in capital. For fiscal 2026, interest was imputed
on the daily outstanding loan balance at the monthly short-term Applicable Federal Rate published by the Internal Revenue Service, which
ranged from 3.56% to 4.10% per annum during the year. In prior years, interest was imputed at a fixed rate of 5.25% per annum. Because
market interest rates were not stable during fiscal 2026, management concluded that a monthly rate better reflects a market rate for the
loan; the change was accounted for prospectively from September 1, 2025 as a change in accounting estimate. Imputed interest expense of
$8,680 and $9,898 for the years ended August 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively, was recorded as additional paid-in capital.

notes.title: Income Taxes
text: Note 8 – Income Taxes
At August 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company had
net operating loss carryforwards for federal income tax purposes of approximately $212,742 and $93,446, respectively, available to offset
future taxable income. Net operating losses arising in tax years beginning after December 31, 2017 may be carried forward indefinitely
but may offset no more than 80% of taxable income in any year. Imputed interest on the related party loan (Note 6) is not deductible for
income tax purposes and is treated as a permanent difference; cumulative imputed interest through August 31, 2026 was $25,483. Amortization
of intangible assets for income tax purposes is the same as for financial reporting purposes, and accordingly no temporary difference
arises. Because realization of the related future tax benefits is not considered more likely than not, no benefit has been recognized
in these financial statements, and a full valuation allowance has been recorded against the associated deferred tax asset.
The valuation allowance totaled approximately
$44,676 at August 31, 2026, reflecting a net increase of $25,052 during the year. Management assesses the realizability of deferred tax
assets by evaluating whether it is more likely than not that some or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized, considering
the scheduled reversal of deferred tax liabilities, projected future taxable income, and available tax planning strategies. Based on this
assessment, management concluded that sufficient uncertainty exists to warrant a full valuation allowance as of August 31, 2026. All tax
years since the Company's inception remain open to examination by taxing authorities.
